native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA on the forms of capital computed in hundred-year time slices, the PC1 value at the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is markedly HIGHER than at all subsequent horizons between 1000 and 500 BCE: a positive spike at the start of the period followed by a steady decline (base case: PC1(1100) = +4.45 vs +2.17 at 1000 BCE, +1.65 at 900, +1.91 at 800, +1.25 at 700, +0.83 at 600, +0.82 at 500 BCE; mean 1000-500 BCE ≈ +1.44, excess ≈ +3.0). The direction is robust across PCA on all 39 slices, YBA-only PCA (where 1100 BCE is the extreme high-capital outlier), re-standardized PCA, and PCA without the constant Sickle variable. PC1 loads positively on capital-intensive indicators (copper/gold, depot, hatchet/sword, pottery decoration, house size), so the 1100 BCE spike reflects an anomalously high level of accumulated/material capital. Caveat: the high 1100 BCE value is partly an interpolation artifact — 7 of 12 indicators are identical to the 1200 BCE slice (carry-over of the last Late Bronze Age observations across a data gap), so part of the spike may reflect forward persistence of interpolated values rather than a genuine 1100 BCE signal.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/capital.csv (decimal comma -> dot), dropped group/color; 39 pre-built 100-year slices, 12 Z-variables. 2) Verified slices are snapshots of the interpolated (*_inter) columns of time_series_data.csv at 100-year marks; identified carry-over of 7/12 variables from 1200 to 1100 BCE. 3) PCA (numpy SVD) in 4 variants: A all 39 slices, B YBA-only 7 slices, C all slices re-standardized, D all slices without constant ZSichel. 4) Compared PC1 at 1100 BCE against each 1000-500 BCE horizon (relative comparison; sign convention neutral). 5) Added pollen openness context (MEAN, SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) at the same horizons (coverage ends at 702 BCE).
